facts.text: The T-Casual multi-trip travel card (10 rides) is shared across metro/bus/tram and is meaningfully cheaper per ride than buying single tickets.

Paella served at restaurants directly on La Rambla is almost universally poor quality, pre-made, and overpriced — genuine paella (which takes about 20 minutes to cook to order) is found in Barceloneta or Poble Sec instead.
Park Güell's monumental zone requires a timed-entry ticket booked in advance (it isn't a normal free park); the surrounding park areas outside that zone remain free.
A weekday "menú del día" lunch (3 courses plus a drink) at neighborhood restaurants is typically €13-18 and much better value than the same restaurant's dinner menu.
Pickpocketing is a genuine, well-documented risk on La Rambla, the metro, and around Sagrada Família — not just tourist paranoia; keep bags zipped and to the front in these areas.
Catalan cuisine leans on seafood and pork; vegetarian tapas exist widely but ask specifically, since many "vegetable" tapas are cooked in the same oil/pans as meat dishes at traditional spots.
Sagrada Família requires timed-entry tickets booked well in advance (weeks, not days, in peak season) — walk-up tickets are frequently sold out.
